strengths: Comprehensive empirical validation of attention low-rank structure across multiple model families, datasets, and layers with multiple converging metrics
Clever decomposition analysis (Section 4.3) isolating W^O anisotropy as the source of low-rank structure
Addresses a real practical problem (dead features) with a simple, effective solution that scales to 1M features
Extensive implementation details, ablations, and pseudo-code support reproducibility
Honest discussion of limitations and edge cases (JumpReLU failures, residual stream limitations) in appendices
Extension to multiple sparse dictionary learning methods (SAEs, Lorsa) demonstrates generalizability of the core insight
weaknesses: Causality between low-rank structure and dead features is observed but not mechanistically explained—no causal experiments with synthetic activations or theoretical analysis provided
Proposed method (PCA initialization) is incremental novelty—essentially applying existing PCsInit (Phan et al. 2025) to SAEs

Critical disconnect between improvements: reconstruction quality improves substantially but downstream Delta LM loss barely improves (Figure 6 note), questioning practical utility for interpretability

Significant limitations underemphasized in main text: (1) ASI fails with high-ℓ₀ warm-up schedules for JumpReLU SAEs (Appendix H), (2) produces more dead features than AuxK at extreme scale (1M features, Figure 7b), (3) minimal gains on high-rank activations like residual streams
Missing analysis of whether W^O anisotropy is inherent to multi-head attention or an avoidable design choice—no exploration of whether different W^O learning could reduce the low-rank structure
Hyperparameter d_init lacks principled selection guidance; claimed 'wide range' (256-2048 for 4096D) shows significant performance variation; unclear how to set for new architectures
Limited downstream validation: no experiments showing whether improved SAE reconstructions lead to better feature interpretability or other downstream benefits

strengths: Novel and well-documented empirical finding: Low effective rank (~60%) of attention outputs demonstrated convincingly across 4 model families, multiple datasets, layers, and activation positions with three complementary metrics (effective rank, singular spectra, loss recovery)

Strong mechanistic analysis: Decomposition (Figure 4) clearly shows W^O's role in dimensionality reduction, with intuitive explanation of overlapping attention head subspaces supported by cross-model evidence

Practical solution with dramatic improvements: Active Subspace Initialization reduces dead features from 87% to <1% at 1M features, shows consistent gains across 16K-1M feature scales, and improves reconstruction quality (normalized MSE ~0.27 vs ~0.31)

Comprehensive experimental validation: Statistical significance testing (Welch's t-test, all p<1e-6), cross-layer/model/dataset evaluation (Tables 6-7), ablation studies (random vs active subspace), feature quality analysis (monosemanticity), and error analysis for stability

Excellent reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, pseudo-code provided, multiple experimental setups with 15-seed significance testing, clear descriptions of metrics, error analysis confirming 10M token stability
Method generalizes beyond SAEs: Successfully applied to Lorsa (sparse replacement models) with similar dead feature reductions, demonstrating broader applicability

Honest limitations discussion: Authors clearly acknowledge unresolved causal mechanism, edge cases with certain training schedules (high initial L0), performance at extreme scales, and appropriate use conditions
weaknesses: Causality unestablished: Paper demonstrates strong correlation between low effective rank and dead features (Figure 5, Tables 1-3) but provides no mechanistic explanation for *why* low-rank geometry causes dead features; missing experimental validation (e.g., artificially inducing low-rankness to test if dead features increase)

Incomplete mechanistic understanding: Why does W^O become anisotropic during training? Is this fundamental or an artifact of specific choices? No analysis of whether this emerges during training or exists from initialization, despite claims it 'may reflect a more fundamental property'

ASI method limitations inadequately characterized: Fails with high initial L0 training schedules (Figures 15-16) requiring ad-hoc PCA preprocessing workaround; at extreme scales (1M features, Figure 8b) produces more dead features than AuxK baseline though reconstruction better; d_init hyperparameter lacks principled guidance

SparseAdam interaction analysis incomplete: Best results require ASI *and* SparseAdam, but contribution from each is unclear; SparseAdam addresses stale momentum (orthogonal concern) but relationship to low-rank structure unexplored; unclear if methods truly orthogonal or if interaction is significant

Limited characterization of ASI applicability: Yields minimal gains on near-full-rank activations (Figure 13), but systematic analysis missing; 'when to use ASI' acknowledged as unclear; boundaries of applicability (TopK yes, TopK-anneal no; JumpReLU conditional) not systematically mapped

Theoretical gaps: Overlapping subspaces explanation intuitive but not rigorously proven; no analysis of feature evolution during training or whether features drift from active subspace; missing connection between dimensionality and optimization landscape

Scope limitations: Only language models (vision transformers untested); models ≤8B parameters; limited multilingual testing; no analysis of potential architectural solutions (Section 6 mentions but doesn't explore)

Experimental inconsistencies: Figures 7-9 use 3 random seeds while significance testing uses 15 seeds; effect sizes inconsistently reported; computational cost of SVD initialization not discussed; some interpretation gaps for ablations

strengths: Novel and rigorously demonstrated empirical finding that attention outputs are confined to surprisingly low-dimensional subspaces (~60% effective rank) across multiple model families, datasets, and layers with three complementary metrics providing convergent validity

Exceptional experimental rigor with statistical significance testing (Welch's t-test, p-values <10^-6 across 15 seeds), thorough ablation studies, and detailed error analysis (CV of 1.5×10^-4), enabling confident conclusions

Clear mechanistic insight via Figure 4's variance decomposition showing the output projection matrix W^O plays a key role in compressing multi-head activations, with intuitive explanation via overlapping subspace superposition

Practical and scalable solution (ASI) that dramatically reduces dead features from 87% to <1% at 1M features with zero additional computational overhead, and generalizes to other sparse dictionary methods (Lorsa, transcoders)
Excellent reproducibility with extensive hyperparameter documentation, pseudocode in appendices, multiple random seeds, and clear implementation details enabling straightforward reproduction
Well-structured presentation with effective visualizations and logical flow from phenomenon observation through problem identification to solution
weaknesses: Causality between low-rank structure and dead features remains unresolved despite strong correlation—paper cannot definitively explain why random initialization fails in low-rank spaces or rule out reverse causality, limiting conceptual depth

Method limitations inadequately emphasized: ASI produces more dead features than AuxK at extreme scales (Figure 8b), fails with high-ℓ₀ warm-up schedules (Appendix L), and requires orthogonal combination with SparseAdam for best results, suggesting it is not a complete solution

Limited theoretical understanding of why attention specifically exhibits low-rank structure while MLPs do not, despite both operating on full-rank residual streams; superposition explanation is intuitive but incomplete
Scope limited to language models only—claims of 'universality' lack validation on vision transformers, BERT-style encoders, or other architectures despite stating robustness across diverse settings

Underdeveloped analysis of practical and conceptual implications: paper does not explore whether low-rank structure is necessary for model function, investigate architectural improvements, or deeply examine downstream consequences for model behavior and efficiency

Feature quality analysis (monosemanticity in Appendix N.1) limited to 100 samples with no comparison of learned semantics between TopK and ASI, and hyperparameter d_init=768 chosen empirically without principled justification despite Figure 6 showing wide acceptable range

Hyperparameter sensitivity and practical requirements underspecified: SVD computation requires 10M tokens for stability (Appendix C), dead feature definition (10M token threshold) shows no sensitivity analysis, and scaling of SVD computational cost not thoroughly analyzed

Method shows activation-dependent efficacy with minimal gains on high-rank activations (residual streams, Appendix J.2), and fails under certain training schedules, limiting the scope of applicability claims
